notes: Fictional subject and object: a made-up class (Tovrish verbs of motion) and a made-up morpheme (the Tovrish prefix 'drovka-', renamed from 'ka-' in review: 'ka-'/'-ka-' is a real past or narrative-tense marker (Swahili, Tagalog) and can't carry a near-zero count, so the object would not honestly be made up) in the real relation past_formed_with. Derived queries apply the rule to verbs named in the prompt; Q1 and Q4 use the everyday fact that running is motion, Q3 a subclass stated in the prompt, Q4 a past event (temporal). All determinate. Near query asks the real 'run'/'ran'. Q1 and Q4 rest on two facts the prompt leaves out, stated in their chains since 2026-10-31: running is a kind of motion (now their bridge, with a check; 'ulveskarn' means 'to run' is a chain step given in the prompt) and the definitional step that a Tovrish verb meaning a motion is a verb of motion (owl/FINDINGS.md C5).
